title: Tenant Visibility Pulse: compact overlay for Private Console
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, dockable overlay ('Visibility Pulse') for the Private/VPC Console that surfaces per-tenant connectivity health, current rollout state, and a cost-velocity indicator in a single glance. The overlay should be usable from cluster and tenant list views and support quick investigation (2-click drilldown) into network egress, recent upgrade jobs, and KV cache hit rates. Goal: reduce mean-time-to-detect for tenant-network incidents and give operators fast rollback/route decisions without leaving context.

decisions: Overlay will be dockable to right-hand side of Console and available in cluster list + tenant detail pages.
Two display densities: 'Pulse' (single-row compact) and 'Expanded Drawer' (full details + charts).
Polling strategy: 30s list refresh, websocket for expanded drawer to stream critical events.
Show cost-velocity as relative sparkline + a projected 24h spend delta; only estimated tokens and egress cost (no PII).
Will include 'Pause rollout' quick action; destructive actions require confirmation modal and link to audit log entry.
Keep visual language aligned with Console color tokens; use new 'safety' amber variant for canary states.
tradeoffs: Compactness vs discoverability: single-row pulse hides detailed metrics; mitigated with hover affordances and clear CTA to expand.
Realtime fidelity vs cost: chose limited polling to reduce backend load; this will slightly delay detection for non-expanded views.
Privacy vs usefulness: no raw token content is surfaced; some debugging signals (raw request IDs) only in expanded drawer after RBAC check.
Cross-cluster UX: representing tenants spanning clusters required a summarization heuristic — we aggregate by worst-state for visibility, with per-cluster breakdown in drawer.
Mobile: overlay is not shown on narrow screens by default; we provide a tenant-card variant in mobile list to surface top-1 issue.
Accessibility vs visual density: increased type sizes for AA contrast reduces compactness slightly but improves usability for oncall engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Pulse appears in cluster list and tenant list rows with correct tenant health color and tooltip descriptions.
Clicking the pulse opens the expanded drawer with three sections: connectivity timeline, rollout jobs (with canary state), and cost-velocity sparkline.
Quick actions are present: View Logs (links to logs), Pause Rollout (requires confirm modal), and Open Audit (links to audit log).
Telemetry: aggregated snapshot API responds within 200ms (p95) for 1K tenants; ENG provides endpoint mock for QA.
Accessibility: keyboard focusable, AA contrast, screen-reader labels for each micro-panel.
